text:
People Ops: Heads-up everyone 1 1 We've published two related updates: 1) temporary emergency PTO carryover exception for serious personal/medical events, and 2) a short travel code-of-conduct reminder for out-of-office meetings. Policy links + manager one-pager here: https://redwood.internal/policies/pto-carryover-exception and https://redwood.internal/policies/travel-code. Quick Q&A in-thread.

rafael_lead: Quick question 1 what's the carryover exception?

People Ops: TL;DR  for qualifying emergencies (serious illness, bereavement, or sudden caregiving duties) employees may request to carry over up to 10 additional PTO days beyond the standard cap for one calendar year. Requests are evaluated case-by-case; supporting info required (one-sentence description + dates). Retroactive exceptions allowed back to 2025-10-01.

emma_finance: How will this show on payroll and accrual reports?

People Ops: The extra days are recorded as "PTO-exception" in HRIS and reconciled during annual accrual processing. Finance note: exceptions don't change benefit eligibility; they are administrative carryovers. We'll surface a summary export for payroll teams labeled PCX-EXCEPTIONS.

newhire_sam: I'm new  am contractors eligible?

People Ops: This policy is for full-time employees only. Contractors should talk to their hiring manager about local options.

rafael_lead: Who approves exceptions? Managers or People Ops?

People Ops: Managers can provisionally approve up to 3 days; anything beyond that routes to People Ops for final approval. Use the Exception Request form on the policy page. Manager approvals should include a short note about operational coverage plans.

travel_team: Separate note on travel code-of-conduct: when traveling on Redwood business you must follow local laws, vendor venue rules, and Redwood's workplace behavior standards. We've added a one-page quick checklist for tradeshows and customer dinners. Link: https://redwood.internal/policies/travel-code#checklist

security_bot: Reminder: If you're traveling with company devices, enable full-disk encryption and use the VPN when connecting to public Wi-Fi. Report lost devices immediately: security@redwood.internal.

People Ops: A few extra clarifications: 1) emergencies only  routine scheduling or poor planning won't qualify; 2) evidence: a brief note and any relevant confirmation (medical note optional) are fine; 3) timeline: submit within 30 days of the start of the emergency for fastest handling.

emma_finance: Tax reminder: depending on local rules, an advance or one-off payment might have tax implications. Finance will attach region-specific tax guidance in the claim acknowledgement email.

rafael_lead: Can managers request retroactive exceptions on behalf of folks who were out and didn't know about this?

People Ops: Yes, managers can submit retroactive requests with supporting details; employee consent required. We prioritized back to 2025-10-01 to capture recent cases.

newhire_sam: If someone uses the carryover, do they lose the extra days if they leave?

People Ops: Carryover days are not paid out on termination except where local law requires payout. If an employee leaves before using the carryover, standard termination pay rules apply.

travel_team: For conference travel specifically: do not accept or solicit gifts that would influence business decisions. If a sponsor offers meals or events, disclose on the expense form. There's a quick field now on the Travel Expense form to mark sponsored items.

People Ops: We'll host a 20-min manager briefing next Friday at 9am PT to walk through examples and form flow. Invite posted to #people-ops-calendar. Manager one-pager attached on both policy pages.

People Ops: Ops bot publishing the docs now. If you have an urgent case, DM People Ops and include "URGENT EXCEPTION" in the subject. We'll triage within 24 hours. :white_check_mark:
